sources.entry: FilesNest - One-way, resumable sync of macOS Photos libraries to self-hosted or local storage.

summary.one_liner: FilesNest mirrors a Mac's Photos library one-way to a self-hosted server, a local folder, or a mounted drive, using resumable uploads.
summary.what_it_does: The macOS menu bar app continuously syncs photos and videos from the Photos library to either a self-hosted FilesNest server or a local folder or mounted drive. Uploads use the TUS resumable upload protocol, so interrupted transfers can continue. Assets are streamed directly without temp files or whole-file buffering. The app keeps no local database; the server decides what needs syncing. Sync progress, counts, and failed items are shown, and syncing can be paused, resumed, or triggered manually. The server is a single Go binary, typically run via Docker Compose with Caddy for automatic HTTPS. The README states that deletions on the Mac are mirrored to the server, so it is not an archival backup.
use_cases: back up Mac Photos library to own server
sync Photos library to external drive or NAS
mirror iCloud-independent photo copies to local folder
how_to_run: Download docker-compose.yml and Caddyfile to a server folder
DOMAIN=backup.example.com BACKUP_USER=admin BACKUP_PASS=changeme docker compose up -d
stack: Swift (macOS app, implied by macOS menu bar app)
notable: One-way mirror that deletes server copies when photos are deleted on the Mac
Resumable TUS uploads for large files and flaky connections
Can sync to a local folder or mounted drive without any server
Prebuilt server image for NAS platforms like Umbrel, TrueNAS, and Unraid
Credentials stored in the macOS Keychain
caveats: Not an archival backup: deleting a photo on the Mac removes its server copy
Self-hosting needs a domain and Docker setup for HTTPS (or a platform reverse proxy); full config is in server/README.md
keywords: backup photos to my own server
